content: To test the performance of our models on real-world conditions, we use commercially available ASR services (Google and IBM) to transcribe the $\mathcal {D}_{test}$ files and measure the performance of our models without assuming any annotations (except when calculating the metrics). It should be noted that this is not the case in our previous evaluations using `10% test' dataset where we use the segmentation information. For ground truth annotations on ASR transcripts, we aligned the MR tags from human written transcripts to the ASR transcript using their grounded timing information. Additionally, since ASR is prone to errors, during the alignment, if a medication from an MR tag is not recognized correctly in the ASR transcript, we remove the corresponding MR tag.
